description: A bank of resonant filters tuned to the harmonic series over lofrq, applied to the input (mode 1 HARMONIC; modes 2-6 give alternate/sub-harmonics and equal-interval banks and are separate curations). Output duration is exactly indur + tail, and the tail flag has an UNDOCUMENTED default of 1.0 s (verified: 2 s in -> 3.0 s out with no -t; 1 s -> 2.0 s; -t2 -> +2 s; -t0.5 -> +0.5 s; the entry pins tail=1.0 explicitly so the model always holds). Q may vary over time (breakpoint verified: differs from both endpoint renders); every other parameter refuses breakpoint files. With scat > 0 the filter frequencies are randomised and the process becomes GENUINELY STOCHASTIC with NO seed flag (two -s0.5 runs 1.1 s apart differ; scat 0 runs are identical) - leave scat at 0 when reproducibility matters. Mono and stereo accepted.
musical_use: Turns any material into a pitched resonance: set lofrq to the fundamental you want and the bank rings its harmonic series through the sound - noise becomes a chord, percussion becomes tuned mallets. Q is the character knob: low Q (1-20) colours while keeping the source recognisable; high Q (hundreds to thousands, afta8 default 400) rings long pitched tails from transients - raise gain substantially at high Q (values of 40-50+ are normal, per the manual) since narrow bands remove most energy. A time-varying Q breakpoint morphs from coloured noise to pure ringing across the file. hifrq caps how many harmonics sound - keep it high (several kHz) for brightness, low for dark hums. scat detunes the series toward bell-like inharmonicity (1 = fully scattered - but unseeded, every render differs). tail lets high-Q rings decay; -d doubles the filtering for steeper isolation.

q.description: Filter tightness (CDP-enforced 0.001 to 10000; 0.0005 refused quoting that range). Low = broad colouring, high = ringing resonators. Banner-confirmed time-variable and verified: a 5->500 breakpoint ran and differs from both endpoint renders.

gain.description: Overall makeup gain (CDP-enforced 0.001 to 10000; 0 refused). High Q needs high gain (40-50+ per the manual). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').

lof.description: Fundamental of the harmonic series (the bank's root). DIVERGENCE: banner/manual give the range as 0-or-10 to srate/3 (14700 at 44.1 kHz); the binary enforces 0.1 to 22050 (probed: 0 and -5 refused quoting '(0.100000 to 22050.000000)'; 5 and 20000 accepted). Breakpoint refused (parameter 3).

hif.description: Upper frequency limit of the bank - harmonics above this are omitted. Same real range as lof (0.1 to 22050; the banner's 'lofrq+ to srate/3' is not enforced, and hif < lof is accepted silently). Breakpoint refused (parameter 4).

tail.description: Decay time appended after the input for the filters to ring out; output duration is exactly indur + tail. CDP's implicit default is 1.0 s (undocumented - the manual omits -t entirely); the entry emits -t1.0 explicitly. CDP-enforced range 0 to 20, but tail = 0 triggers a buffer bug (output balloons to a fixed 262144 frames with a garbage-silence tail) - curated minimum 0.01 keeps it unreachable. Breakpoint refused.

scat.description: Random scatter of the filter frequencies away from the exact harmonic series (CDP-enforced 0 to 1; 2 refused). NON-REPRODUCIBLE: there is no seed flag and two identical scat>0 commands produce different output (verified 1.1 s apart); scat 0 (or omitting the flag) is fully deterministic. Breakpoint refused.

double.description: Double filtering - the bank is applied with a steeper effective rolloff (verified: changes the render, duration unchanged).

examples.description: Ring a 110 Hz harmonic chord out of noise, with a ringing decay.
examples.expected_use: Pitched, bell-organ resonance at A2; output = indur + 2 s.

examples.description: Morph from coloured noise to pure ringing via time-varying Q.
examples.expected_use: Breakpoint Q (relative times); tail defaults to 1.0 s, so output = indur + 1.

known_issues: BINARY-VINTAGE HANG (macOS QA 2026-07-15): filter binaries built before the upstream fix of 2025-06-05 (CDP8 commit 11cdcb4, 'fixed alloc bug for fixed filter bank') perform an out-of-bounds heap write on EVERY bank run - the code writes internal params FLT_TIMES_CNT (index 20) and FLT_FRQ_INDEX (index 21), but the fixed bank only allocates internal params '000diiiiid' (those slots exist only for the varybanks). Undefined behavior: the shipped macOS r8 binary hangs (>120 s on a 2 s input the post-fix Linux build completes in 0.00 s); crashes or silent corruption are equally possible on other heap layouts. bank is the only curated filter mode that runs the normalization pre-pass containing the write (sweeping/lohi unaffected). Fix: rebuild filter from current CDP8 source. This is why version_sensitive is true.

UNDOCUMENTED DEFAULT (first-class finding): with no -t flag the binary appends a 1.0 s tail - neither the banner nor cgrofilt.htm mentions a default, and the manual's usage line omits -t altogether. The entry pins tail=1.0 explicitly so the duration model indur + tail is always exact (verified sample-exact across 1/2/3 s inputs and tails 0.5-2).

tail = 0 is accepted by CDP (range 0-20) but is buggy: output becomes a fixed 262144 frames (2^18, about 5.94 s at 44.1 kHz) regardless of input length, the extension carrying low-level filter garbage (verified on 1 s and 2 s inputs; first section matches the normal render). Curated minimum 0.01 avoids it.
scat > 0 is genuinely stochastic with NO seed: two identical commands 1.1 s apart differ. Keep scat = 0 for reproducible renders; there is no way to pin a take.
DIVERGENCE: lof/hif's real enforced range is 0.1 to 22050 Hz, not the documented 10 (or 0) to srate/3; and hif < lof passes silently.

Only Q accepts breakpoint files; gain/lof/hif/tail/scat refuse with 'Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.' (N = 2,3,4; tail and scat report 6 and 7 in the brk-read stage but 5 and 6 in range refusals - CDP's numbering is stage-dependent).
Deterministic with scat unset (two runs identical in decoded samples).
